dataset_attribution_citations.note: The remaining 17 in-text citations are all in Table 1's Dataset column, each attributing one dataset to its origin paper (citation_rules.md §3: 'Our approach is inspired by [S]'-style attribution is fine when true; here it is the stronger 'cite the creators of an existing asset' case, hard rule 4a-equivalent). For each: step 1 (exists) and step 2 (metadata) pass against project/paper.txt's own reference-list entry; step 3 (supports) passes trivially, since the citation's sole role is to attribute the dataset it names, and that attribution matches project/paper.txt's own Appendix D usage; step 4 (strength) passes, no claim beyond attribution is made; step 5 (status) is recorded per source in corpus/source_registry.json; step 6 (primary) passes, each is the dataset's own introducing paper; step 7 (purpose) passes, the purpose (attribution) is exactly what the table cell is for; step 8 (integrity) was not checked (no retraction-database access this run).
dataset_attribution_citations.note_on_quora: Quora is listed in Table 1 with no citation, matching project/paper.txt itself, which gives no bracket reference for the Quora Duplicate Questions dataset. No citation was invented.

summary: 0 UNVERIFIED_CITATION failures. Every citation resolves to a project/paper.txt reference-list entry with a location where it is actually used; none is decorative (every one states or supports a specific fact); no sentence's claim strength exceeds its cited source's own (checked explicitly for the two hedged/speculative citations, Guo et al. 2020 / Petroni et al. 2020 for the scoped novelty claim, and Hofstätter et al. 2021 for the speculative TAS-B attribution). Reference-list <-> in-text cross-check (done separately, see claim_evidence_audit.md) found a perfect 34/34 match in both directions.
